title: TritonWorks - Burst SLA discovery
summary: Discovery call to align on TritonWorks' latency (p95) SLAs, concurrency and burst behavior, streaming vs non-streaming paths, and whether Hosted/Dedicated/Private best fits their compliance profile. Customer requested a benchmark run with representative prompts and wants cost/throughput estimates for a Dedicated pilot and a Private (VPC) option for regulated customers. Agreed next steps: run a controlled token/sec benchmark, share security docs, and provide tailored pricing for a 3-month pilot.
topics: p95 latency targets for short chat and long responses
Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private tradeoffs
security/compliance: SOC2, KMS, audit logs, SSO
action_items: Samira Khan - Send tailored pricing sheet for 3-month Dedicated pilot + burst add-on - 2027-12-02
Diego Alvarez - Stand up benchmark plan and share spreadsheet template + sample prompts - 2027-12-01
Priya Patel - Share security pack (SOC2 report, KMS integration notes, VPC checklist) - 2027-12-03
Ethan Ross - Provide 3 representative prompt sets and expected 95th pct token lengths - 2027-12-01
next_steps: Schedule benchmark window (2 hours) for 2027-12-06 to run throughput and streaming tests
Redwood to provide pricing & pilot contract by 2027-12-02
Customer to confirm list of regulated customers that would require Private deployment by 2027-12-07
transcript:
Meeting header: Date: 2027-11-29; Start: 15:00 PST; Duration: 48m; Attendees: Samira Khan (Redwood AE), Diego Alvarez (Redwood SE), Priya Patel (Redwood SE), Ethan Ross (CTO), Nora Chen (Head of ML), Luis Martinez (Platform), Rachel Lim (VP Security)

Summary (auto): Quick discovery to map p95 targets, concurrency, and streaming expectations. Customer leaning Dedicated for performance predictability, Private for regulated enterprise deals. Agreed to benchmark and share security docs.

[00:00] Samira (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for making time. Quick roll call — I see Ethan, Nora, Luis, Rachel — can you confirm?
[00:06] Ethan (TritonWorks): Yep, Ethan here. Morning from SF.
[00:08] Nora (TritonWorks): Nora here, thanks.
[00:10] Luis (TritonWorks): Luis.
[00:11] Rachel (TritonWorks): Rachel on for security.
[00:13] Samira: Great. We'll keep this tight — goal is to understand your p95 latency targets and burst patterns so we can recommend Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private. Diego and Priya are with me on the technical side.
[00:20] Diego (Redwood SE): Hi all — I'll focus on throughput and streaming tradeoffs.
[00:24] Nora: To kick off, our product is real-time clinical triage chat for enterprise partners. For short turn prompts (user utterance -> 30 tokens) we need p95 under 200ms. For longer, streamed assistant responses (400-1,200 tokens) we need p95 under 2.5s end-to-end. Peak concurrency is... complicated — baseline 300 concurrent active users, typical burst spikes to ~1,800 for campaign events.
[00:44] Samira: Cool, that helps. When you say p95 under 200ms for short chats, is that including network hop from your app to our hosted region and back, or is that just server-side compute?
[00:52] Ethan: The SLAs we promise customers are end-to-end. So assume network + compute. We'll be on GCP in us-west1.
[00:58] Diego: Understood. For Hosted we can put you in us-west region; Dedicated gives you isolated GPU pools so predictable p95 under load; Private (VPC/on-prem) is an option for regulated customers but adds ops overhead.
[01:10] Luis: Curious about streaming — we're trying to keep perceived latency low for long responses by streaming tokens as they generate. What's Redwood's approach there? Any difference in p95 measurement?
[01:18] Priya (Redwood SE): Streaming is typically measured by time-to-first-byte and token throughput. We optimize KV cache and prefix caching to reduce repeated compute. The p95 for time-to-first-byte is usually much lower than full-response p95; we can configure to prioritize first-token latency.
[01:30] Nora: What's realistic for time-to-first-byte for a 1,024-context model on Dedicated vs Hosted?
[01:35] Diego: On Dedicated we often see first-token p95 in sub-150ms for common models at short context lengths; with longer context it increases — maybe 180-250ms. Hosted depends on multi-tenant load but we show percentile performance in the portal. For sustained bursts you'll want Dedicated.
[01:48] Rachel: On security: our compliance team requires SOC2 Type II, KMS integration for customer keys, audit logs, and SSO with SAML. Private deployment would be preferred for higher-risk customers.
[01:57] Samira: We can support KMS/HSM integrations and SAML. Priya will share the security pack after the call.
[02:03] Nora: For benchmarking: we need token/sec numbers so we can cost out — what's the baseline tokens/sec per GPU for your recommended quantized variants?
[02:11] Diego: It varies by model and quantization; ballpark — for medium-sized 7B-ish models you can expect 600-1,200 tok/s per GPU under continuous generation; for 13B+ models it's lower, 200-600 tok/s depending on sequence length and batch config. But real workloads with many short prompts benefit from batching and caching.
[02:27] Ethan: We have a mix — short chats (32 tokens) dominate 70% of calls, long responses ~20%, embeddings/other ~10%.
[02:35] Samira: That mix helps — Diego can size a Dedicated pool for steady-state plus burst headroom. What's your desired safety margin on bursts? 2x? 3x?
[02:41] Nora: Historically we plan for 2.5x peak. So if you say 1,800 bursts, we want comfort up to 4,500 concurrent short-chat sessions.
[02:50] Diego: Ok that is a meaningful number. For pure short-chat workloads, with batching we can get high throughput, but the p95 target under 200ms including network is tight at 4.5k concurrent. We'd probably recommend Dedicated with autoscaling and a burst reserve, maybe a combination of Dedicated + edge cache for prefixes.
[03:06] Luis: Are there options to trade cost for latency — e.g., lower quantization for lower latency or more GPUs?
[03:12] Priya: Yes. We provide quantization profiles and model variant recommendations. For low-latency critical paths you can run a less-quantized variant or smaller context windows. Also routing policy can send critical traffic to Dedicated and less critical to Hosted.
[03:24] Ethan: For regulated customers, we'd need Private with VPC peering and audit logs. How long to deploy Private?
[03:30] Samira: Private VPC deployments typically take 4-8 weeks depending on network approvals, certs, and KMS setup. On-prem is longer. There's a private control plane option to reduce customer ops.
[03:40] Rachel: Ok. Can you also confirm data residency options — we need UK/EU for a handful of customers.
[03:45] Priya: Yes we have EU and US regions for Hosted, Dedicated can be provisioned in EU regions. We'll document region SLAs.
[03:52] Nora: Back to benchmarks — we'd like Redwood to run a throughput/sustained burst test with our prompts. Ideally: (1) 30-token short chat at 1k concurrent baseline, (2) ramp to 4.5k over 10 minutes, (3) streaming long-response test 200 concurrent with 800 tok/s aggregated.
[04:10] Diego: That's doable. We'll need the prompt sets and expected token lengths. We'll run on a Dedicated mirror and capture p95, p99, token/sec, and time-to-first-byte. We'll share a spreadsheet with columns for model, quant, batch size, tokens/sec, p50/p95/p99.
[04:22] Samira: We'll include cost estimates per token and per-hour Dedicated node for the pilot. What's the normal pilot duration you run for these customers?
[04:29] Diego: We typically do a 30–90 day pilot — 90 days is common for enterprise to validate production behavior. For strict SLAs we do a 90-day pilot with monitoring and two scheduled failover drills.
[04:40] Luis: Concern: how does Redwood handle graceful degradation if Dedicated capacity saturates? Do you have automatic fallback to Hosted or model variants?
[04:47] Priya: Yes — routing policies can fail over to compatible model variants or to Hosted with throttling rules. We also have circuit-breaker policies to avoid cascading errors. We'll walk you through mapping those to customer SLAs in the runbook.
[04:59] Rachel: About audit logs: retention windows, can we export them to our SIEM?
[05:03] Priya: Yep, audit logs can be exported to your cloud storage or SIEM; retention configurable per account if you're on an enterprise plan.
[05:10] Ethan: Any surprises around tokenizer differences or deterministic token counts during benchmarking? We've seen tokenizer differences affect cost estimates across platforms.
[05:17] Diego: Good call — we can standardize on a tokenizer and include token counts in the benchmark spreadsheet. We'll note tokenization mismatches if they show up.
[05:24] Nora: Any references to similar customers? A short case study would help our execs.
[05:28] Samira: We can share a redacted case study for a healthcare customer that had similar burst patterns and used Dedicated + prefix caching. I'll attach the one-pager.
[05:35] Luis: About pricing — do you charge per-token + per-hour Dedicated node? Any burst add-ons?
[05:40] Samira: For Hosted it's per-token; Dedicated is a reserved capacity model with base monthly + overage on bursts; we can configure a burst reserve (pre-warmed nodes) for predictable spikes. We'll show an example pricing for your workload.
[05:51] Ethan: If we do a pilot, what's the minimum commitment?
[05:54] Samira: For a pilot we usually do a 3-month reserved min for Dedicated to get predictable capacity; we can do month-to-month for Hosted.
[05:59] Nora: Okay thank you. Anything else from Redwood?
[06:03] Diego: One more technical note — streaming token rates are impacted by KV cache hits. If your prompts reuse context, effective throughput improves significantly.
[06:12] Nora: We do reuse templates a lot, so caching should help.
[06:15] Rachel: We'll need the SOC2 docs before moving a subset of customers to Hosted.
[06:19] Priya: We'll send those after the call.
[06:21] Samira: Great. Let's recap next steps. Diego will run a benchmark plan and Samira will send pricing + pilot terms. Priya will send security pack. TritonWorks will send prompt sets and approval for benchmark window.
[06:33] Ethan: Sounds good. Thanks everyone.
[06:35] Samira: Thanks, we'll follow up with calendar invites.

Artifacts referenced: Pricing example deck (link: bit.ly/redwood-pricing-triton), Benchmark spreadsheet template (link: bit.ly/rw-bench-tpl), Security pack (to be sent privately).

Auto-tags: discovery, latency, streaming, dedicated, private, pilot, security

End of transcript.
